topics.title: Linear algebra
topics.summary: Vectors, matrices and the geometry of linear maps.

topics.title: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry
topics.summary: Constructions, invariants and models where the parallel postulate changes.

topics.title: Topology
topics.summary: Open sets, continuity, compactness and loops with hypotheses kept visible.

topics.title: Abstract algebra
topics.summary: Symmetry, groups, rings and the role of structure-preserving maps.

topics.title: Differential geometry
topics.summary: Curves, surfaces, geodesics and curvature from calculus.

topics.title: Algebraic geometry
topics.summary: Polynomial zero sets and a carefully limited path toward affine geometry.

topics.title: Category theory
topics.summary: Objects, arrows and universal constructions in concrete examples.

articles.title: A walk is a vector
articles.hook: Two routes reach the same cafe.
articles.outcome: Add and scale displacement vectors; distinguish a vector from its chosen coordinates.
articles.visual: Head-to-tail arrows beside a coordinate table.
articles.proof: Full proof of component addition from coordinate displacements; defer abstract vector spaces.

editionPrerequisites: signed numbers and coordinate pairs (refreshed here)
metadataProvenance.rationale: Signed coordinates are explicitly refreshed before component arithmetic; the empty catalogue list hid that entry assumption.

prerequisiteLabels: signed numbers and coordinate pairs (refreshed here)

articles.title: Why the dot product measures alignment
articles.hook: How much of a wind pushes along a road?
articles.outcome: Compute a projection and state the nonzero-vector condition.
articles.visual: Angle slider, projected length and signed numeric readout.
articles.proof: Proof sketch from the cosine rule; full derivation offered in a proof drawer.

editionPrerequisites: coordinate pairs and right triangles (refreshed here)
metadataProvenance.rationale: Coordinates and right triangles are refreshed, but the angle identity explicitly assumes the cosine rule rather than proving it.

prerequisiteLabels: coordinate pairs and right triangles (refreshed here)
cosine rule (assumed for the angle identity)

articles.title: A matrix is a rule for moving space
articles.hook: A grid becomes a slanted grid.
articles.outcome: Find a 2×2 map from the images of basis vectors; test linearity.
articles.visual: Grid deformation with image of each basis arrow and a value table.
articles.proof: Full proof by linearity; a drawn grid alone is not the argument.

editionPrerequisites: vector addition and scalar multiplication (refreshed here)
metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule refreshes addition and scalar multiplication; coordinate pairs remain the entry language.

prerequisiteLabels: vector addition and scalar multiplication (refreshed here)

articles.title: When two equations meet
articles.hook: Two constraints may cross, coincide or miss.
articles.outcome: Solve a 2×2 system and interpret zero, one or infinitely many solutions.
articles.visual: Lines and row operations shown in matched panels.
articles.proof: Full proof of equivalence for each reversible row operation.

editionPrerequisites: linear equations and coordinate pairs (refreshed here)
metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule and reversible elimination use linear equations and coordinate pairs, with the notation refreshed locally.

prerequisiteLabels: linear equations and coordinate pairs (refreshed here)

articles.title: What determinant actually counts
articles.hook: Does a map crush a square to a line?
articles.outcome: Compute signed area scaling and use det≠0 to detect invertibility in 2D.
articles.visual: Unit square mapped to parallelogram with oriented area readout.
articles.proof: Full 2D area derivation; higher-dimensional determinant deferred.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The body refreshes matrix columns and parallelogram area and uses coordinate pairs for its signed-area derivation.

articles.title: Missing dimensions have to go somewhere
articles.hook: A camera flattens depth.
articles.outcome: Compute kernel and image for a small map and explain rank-nullity in finite dimensions.
articles.formula: dim ker A+dim im A=dim domain
articles.visual: Input grid collapsing along kernel directions; dimension table.
articles.proof: Full finite-dimensional proof by extending a kernel basis.

editionPrerequisites: linear maps, homogeneous systems and basis (refreshed here)
metadataProvenance.rationale: The body uses homogeneous systems, linear maps and bases, all recalled in its capsule, before a finite-dimensional proof.

prerequisiteLabels: linear maps, homogeneous systems and basis (refreshed here)

articles.title: Coordinates depend on a basis
articles.hook: The same vector has two address systems.
articles.outcome: Change basis in R² and distinguish the vector from its coordinate column.
articles.visual: Two draggable bases and synchronized coordinate tables.
articles.proof: Full proof of coordinate conversion when P is invertible.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule refreshes independence and vector arithmetic before the planar coordinate-change argument.

articles.title: Directions a map does not turn
articles.hook: Stretch a rubber sheet and find unmoved directions.
articles.outcome: Solve simple eigenpairs and explain when a real matrix has no real eigenvectors.
articles.visual: Unit-circle arrows before and after transformation; mark eigenlines.
articles.proof: Full 2×2 characteristic equation; existence in arbitrary dimension deferred.

editionPrerequisites: 2×2 determinant, systems and quadratic equations (refreshed here)
metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule recalls the determinant criterion and homogeneous systems; the calculation additionally needs quadratic equations.

prerequisiteLabels: 2×2 determinant, systems and quadratic equations (refreshed here)

articles.title: The closest answer to an impossible system
articles.hook: Measurements disagree; what fit is best?
articles.outcome: Derive the normal equations for a full-column-rank least-squares problem.
articles.visual: Data points, fitted line and residual orthogonality readout.
articles.proof: Full orthogonality proof under full-column-rank hypothesis; numerical conditioning deferred.

editionPrerequisites: dot product, transpose and systems (refreshed here)
metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule explains transpose and dot products before deriving normal equations for a matrix system.

prerequisiteLabels: dot product, transpose and systems (refreshed here)

articles.title: Rotate, stretch, rotate
articles.hook: A complicated map can have simple principal directions.
articles.outcome: Interpret singular values as axis lengths for a real 2×2 map.
articles.visual: Unit circle to ellipse with axis labels and matrix table.
articles.proof: Proof sketch via eigenvectors of AᵀA; full general spectral theorem deferred.

editionPrerequisites: dot product, eigenvectors and orthogonal matrices (refreshed here)
metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule refreshes orthogonal matrices and eigenvectors, but explicitly invokes the real symmetric 2×2 spectral theorem as an unproved dependency.

prerequisiteLabels: dot product, eigenvectors and orthogonal matrices (refreshed here)
real symmetric 2×2 spectral theorem (used without proof)

articles.title: Why a detour cannot be shorter
articles.hook: Can a bent path beat the direct route?
articles.outcome: Prove the triangle inequality for Euclidean vectors.
articles.visual: Two-segment route and straight route with exact lengths.
articles.proof: Full proof from Cauchy–Schwarz, with its 2D proof supplied locally.

articles.title: A compass bisects an angle
articles.hook: Build an exact half-angle without measuring it.
articles.outcome: Construct an angle bisector and identify the congruence theorem used.
articles.visual: Stepwise compass arcs with labelled equal radii.
articles.proof: Full proof by side-side-side triangle congruence; state ideal straightedge-and-compass assumptions.

articles.title: One parallel axiom, different worlds
articles.hook: What if a line has more than one parallel through a point?
articles.outcome: Separate Euclidean, spherical and hyperbolic parallel claims and the meaning of line in each model.
articles.formula: Euclidean: exactly one parallel through P outside ℓ
articles.visual: Three model cards with line definitions and incidence table.
articles.proof: Proof sketch/model evidence only; consistency and independence require deeper foundations.

articles.title: Where triangle angle sums come from
articles.hook: Every school triangle seems to add to 180°.
articles.outcome: Prove the Euclidean angle-sum theorem and locate its parallel-postulate use.
articles.visual: Triangle with movable vertices and a parallel through one vertex.
articles.proof: Full Euclidean proof; counterexample statement for hyperbolic triangles.

articles.title: Why scale preserves shape
articles.hook: A map and a city block share angles but not lengths.
articles.outcome: Use AA similarity to derive a proportionality equation under Euclidean hypotheses.
articles.visual: Nested similar triangles and side-ratio table.
articles.proof: Full proof from parallel-line intercept theorem; local proof capsule includes that theorem.

articles.title: The angle at the circumference
articles.hook: The same chord seems to subtend the same angle.
articles.outcome: Prove the inscribed-angle theorem for points on one arc.
articles.visual: Circle with moving P and explicit arc restriction.
articles.proof: Full case-based proof; warns that moving P across the chord changes the intercepted arc.

articles.title: Straight lines inside a curved disk
articles.hook: Circular arcs can be geodesics.
articles.outcome: Identify Poincaré disk geodesics and distinguish Euclidean drawing size from hyperbolic distance.
articles.visual: Disk with orthogonal-circle geodesics and sampled distance table.
articles.proof: Proof sketch using disk metric; derivation of all geodesics deferred.

editionPrerequisites: basic integration and logarithms (for the optional distance derivation)
metadataProvenance.rationale: The body allows the radial formula without its integral derivation; integration and logarithms apply to that optional derivation and are labelled accordingly.

prerequisiteLabels: basic integration and logarithms (for the optional distance derivation)

articles.title: Triangle area from missing angle
articles.hook: In the hyperbolic plane, smaller angle sum measures area.
articles.outcome: Use the curvature −1 area formula for a geodesic triangle and state its units.
articles.visual: Geodesic triangle with angle and area readouts.
articles.proof: Proof sketch via Gauss–Bonnet; full theorem deferred.

articles.title: Three right angles on a sphere
articles.hook: A spherical triangle can have three 90° corners.
articles.outcome: Construct the octant triangle and distinguish great-circle geodesics from latitude lines.
articles.visual: Globe model and three great-circle arcs with angle table.
articles.proof: Full verification for octant; general spherical excess theorem deferred.

articles.title: Count area with lattice points
articles.hook: A jagged polygon has an exact area from a count.
articles.outcome: Apply Pick’s theorem to simple lattice polygons and explain why holes need adjustment.
articles.visual: Lattice polygon editor with interior and boundary counts.
articles.proof: Proof sketch by triangulating into primitive lattice triangles; full existence argument deferred.

articles.title: Open means room to move
articles.hook: A point near an edge may still be inside.
articles.outcome: Test openness in R with the metric-ball definition and distinguish open from closed.
articles.visual: Number line and epsilon interval with boundary cases.
articles.proof: Full proofs for standard open and non-open intervals; arbitrary topological spaces deferred.

articles.title: Continuity without drawing a curve
articles.hook: A function can be tested by what it does to open sets.
articles.outcome: Show continuity equivalence with open preimages for maps between metric spaces.
articles.formula: f continuous ⇔ f⁻¹(V) open for every open V
articles.visual: Domain and codomain interval mapping with inverse-image readout.
articles.proof: Full proof in metric spaces; no claim that a plot proves continuity.

articles.title: When two shapes count as the same
articles.hook: Can an interval be stretched into a circle?
articles.outcome: Define homeomorphism and test examples using compactness or cut points.
articles.formula: f:X→Y bijective, f and f⁻¹ continuous
articles.visual: Bendable interval beside circle; endpoint/cut-point table.
articles.proof: Full proof that [0,1] and a circle are not homeomorphic via cut points after defining them.

articles.title: Why finite subcovers matter
articles.hook: An infinite blanket collection may have a finite selection.
articles.outcome: Use open-cover compactness and prove [a,b] is compact in R.
articles.visual: Cover strips on an interval with finite selection log.
articles.proof: Full interval proof using supremum; requires least-upper-bound property of R.

articles.title: A gap you cannot cover up
articles.hook: What makes one piece truly one piece?
articles.outcome: State connectedness by separation and prove continuous images of connected spaces are connected.
articles.formula: X≠U∪V for disjoint nonempty relatively open U,V
articles.visual: Two-color partition trials for interval and union of intervals.
articles.proof: Full proof of image theorem; converse not asserted.

articles.title: Glue edges, change a space
articles.hook: A rectangle can become a cylinder by identifying edges.
articles.outcome: Define quotient topology and verify one cylinder edge-identification example.
articles.formula: V⊂X/~ open ⇔ q⁻¹(V) open in X
articles.visual: Rectangle edge labels and glued cylinder with quotient map readout.
articles.proof: Full verification of the quotient rule; classification of surfaces deferred.

articles.title: What survives triangulation
articles.hook: A cube and a tetrahedron both give two.
articles.outcome: Compute V−E+F for closed triangulated surfaces and name its scope.
articles.visual: Triangulated sphere and torus with live V,E,F table.
articles.proof: Proof sketch of invariance under subdivision; full triangulation-independence deferred.

editionPrerequisites: a simple path or tree (defined here)
metadataProvenance.rationale: Graph terms and spanning trees are introduced locally; counting is the entry skill. The proof is explicitly conditional on a stated plane-separation lemma.

prerequisiteLabels: a simple path or tree (defined here)

articles.title: Can a loop be shrunk?
articles.hook: A loop around a puncture refuses to disappear.
articles.outcome: Define based loop homotopy and contrast disk and punctured-plane examples.
articles.visual: Loop deformation with basepoint and puncture markers.
articles.proof: Proof sketch using winding number for punctured plane; full π₁ computation deferred.

articles.title: Count turns without trusting a picture
articles.hook: A loop can wind twice even while self-crossing.
articles.outcome: Compute winding number for polygonal loops avoiding the origin and state homotopy invariance.
articles.visual: Path editor with unwrapped angle trace and integer readout.
articles.proof: Proof sketch from continuous lifting of argument; lifting theorem deferred.

articles.title: Loops around the circle form integers
articles.hook: Walking around a circle composes like addition.
articles.outcome: State π₁(S¹)≅Z and prove the group law given the lifting lemma.
articles.visual: Circle loop and real-line lift with endpoints and winding readout.
articles.proof: Proof sketch conditional on path and homotopy lifting; full lifting proof deferred.

articles.title: A square as an algebra machine
articles.hook: How many distinct ways can a square be moved onto itself?
articles.outcome: Compose square symmetries and identify identity and inverses.
articles.visual: Square transform buttons and an 8×8 composition table.
articles.proof: Full closure/identity/inverse/associativity argument using composition of bijections.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The body recalls bijections and checks concrete quarter-turn and reflection actions; general angle knowledge alone is too vague.

articles.title: Clock arithmetic is a group
articles.hook: Why does adding hours wrap around?
articles.outcome: Verify the group axioms for addition modulo n and locate additive inverses.
articles.visual: Clock dial and residue table for varying n≥2.
articles.proof: Full proof including well-definedness under congruence classes.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule defines congruence through divisibility and refreshes residue classes before the addition proof.

articles.title: How long until a symmetry returns?
articles.hook: Repeat a rotation until it becomes the identity.
articles.outcome: Compute element order in a finite group and relate it to a cyclic subgroup.
articles.visual: Repeated transformation strip with return counter.
articles.proof: Full proof that powers repeat and form a subgroup in finite groups.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule recalls group operations and identity; the proof explains its pigeonhole step locally.

articles.title: Why subgroup sizes divide
articles.hook: Can a 6-element group contain a 4-element subgroup?
articles.outcome: Apply Lagrange’s theorem and distinguish its converse from the theorem.
articles.visual: Coset partition tiles and exact count.
articles.proof: Full finite-group proof by disjoint equal-sized left cosets.

metadataProvenance.rationale: Groups, subgroups and bijections are recalled before the coset-partition proof.

articles.title: A map that respects the operation
articles.hook: A complicated group may cast a simpler shadow.
articles.outcome: Test homomorphisms and compute kernel/image for Z→Z/nZ.
articles.visual: Input/output Cayley table with operation-preserving squares.
articles.proof: Full verification for modular reduction and kernel subgroup; isomorphism theorem deferred.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule refreshes group maps and modular classes; these are the concrete ingredients of the example.

articles.title: Collapse a normal subgroup
articles.hook: What if all multiples of n count as zero?
articles.outcome: Construct Z/nZ as a quotient and state why normality is required in general groups.
articles.visual: Coset partitions with selected representatives and multiplication result.
articles.proof: Full well-definedness proof for normal subgroups; converse necessity shown.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The body uses subgroup cosets, inverses and representative changes; a prior homomorphism theorem is not an input to its well-definedness proof.

articles.title: Polynomials are numbers with a variable
articles.hook: What algebraic rules survive when coefficients become polynomials?
articles.outcome: Verify key ring rules in R[x] and distinguish polynomial from polynomial function over finite fields.
articles.visual: Coefficient arrays and evaluations over R and F₂.
articles.proof: Full distributivity proof by finite sums; equality-of-functions caveat proved with x²−x over F₂.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule refreshes commutative ring laws and polynomial arithmetic, rather than assuming integer coefficients alone.

articles.title: Remainders as quotient rings
articles.hook: Modulo n is a way to collapse an entire ideal.
articles.outcome: Define ideals in Z and prove every ideal is nZ.
articles.visual: Integer-line multiples, cosets and residue readout.
articles.proof: Full proof using least positive element; zero ideal handled separately.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The integer-ideal proof needs division with remainder and the stated well-ordering principle; ring operations are recalled locally.

articles.title: Why division sometimes fails modulo n
articles.hook: 3 has an inverse mod 7, but 2 fails mod 6.
articles.outcome: Prove Z/nZ is a field exactly when n is prime (n≥2).
articles.visual: Multiplication tables with nonzero inverse highlights.
articles.proof: Full proof using Bézout and zero divisors; Bézout stated with local refresher.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The unit criterion explicitly uses the stated Bézout identity, with a Euclidean-algorithm refresher; gcd alone did not name this input.

articles.title: Why prime powers force subgroups
articles.hook: Group orders can force subgroups to exist.
articles.outcome: State the first Sylow theorem accurately and work one small-order consequence.
articles.visual: Order factorization and subgroup possibility table.
articles.proof: Theorem statement plus worked consequence only; Sylow proof deferred and clearly labelled.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The body recalls Lagrange and applies first Sylow as a stated external theorem to finite groups and prime factorizations.

articles.title: A curve has a speedometer
articles.hook: A bent path is longer than its chord.
articles.outcome: Compute arc length from a smooth parametrization and explain regularity.
articles.visual: Curve with equal-time and equal-distance markers; length readout.
articles.proof: Proof sketch from polygonal approximations for C¹ curves; convergence details deferred.

articles.title: Different clocks, same curve
articles.hook: Walk the same path at a different speed.
articles.outcome: Verify arc-length invariance under smooth increasing reparameterization.
articles.visual: One trace with two time markers and matched cumulative lengths.
articles.proof: Full proof by chain rule and substitution; nonregular pauses discussed separately.

articles.title: How sharply does a curve turn?
articles.hook: A circle and a straight line differ by turning rate.
articles.outcome: Calculate signed curvature of regular plane curves and its value for a circle.
articles.visual: Tangent arrow and osculating-circle approximation with numeric curvature.
articles.proof: Full derivation from derivative of unit tangent for regular C² curves.

articles.title: The moving frame of a plane curve
articles.hook: Carry coordinate axes along a path.
articles.outcome: Use Frenet equations for a unit-speed plane curve and explain sign conventions.
articles.visual: Moving orthonormal frame with signed curvature trace.
articles.proof: Full proof by differentiating T·T and T·N; restricted to oriented plane curves.

articles.title: A surface needs local coordinates
articles.hook: A globe needs more than one flat map.
articles.outcome: Define a regular surface patch and identify coordinate singularities on a sphere.
articles.visual: Sphere coordinate grid with pole warning and derivative table.
articles.proof: Full rank check away from poles; manifold atlas theory deferred.

articles.title: Measuring on a surface
articles.hook: How long is a route drawn on a curved surface?
articles.outcome: Compute local length from the first fundamental form of a parameterized surface.
articles.visual: Parameter-grid route with metric coefficients and numeric length.
articles.proof: Full derivation from dX=X_u du+X_v dv for regular patches.

articles.title: Locally straight on a curved surface
articles.hook: Flights follow great circles on an ideal sphere.
articles.outcome: Define a geodesic by locally stationary length and verify great circles as sphere examples.
articles.visual: Sphere path comparison, local length table and great-circle candidate.
articles.proof: Proof sketch via constrained acceleration; general existence and minimization range deferred.

articles.title: One curvature, two principal bends
articles.hook: A saddle bends both up and down.
articles.outcome: Compute Gaussian curvature for sphere and saddle patches and distinguish intrinsic from extrinsic claims.
articles.visual: Principal normal sections and signed k₁,k₂,K readouts.
articles.proof: Proof sketch of shape-operator computation; Theorema Egregium deferred.

articles.title: Curvature adds up to topology
articles.hook: A sphere has a fixed total bend.
articles.outcome: State Gauss–Bonnet for a compact oriented closed surface and calculate the sphere case.
articles.visual: Triangulated sphere with curvature integral and χ table.
articles.proof: Theorem stated and sphere calculation shown; general proof deferred with hypotheses explicit.

articles.title: A direction can change after a round trip
articles.hook: Carry an arrow around a spherical triangle.
articles.outcome: Compute spherical holonomy for one explicit triangle and relate it to enclosed area.
articles.formula: Δθ≡Area/R² (mod 2π) for a positively oriented simple spherical loop
articles.visual: Arrow transport along octant edges with angle/area readout.
articles.proof: Proof sketch via Gauss–Bonnet for the octant; general holonomy theorem deferred.

articles.title: Draw the solutions of a polynomial
articles.hook: One equation can make a line, circle or cusp.
articles.outcome: Plot real zero loci and distinguish an equation from its set of real solutions.
articles.visual: Equation editor with contour and sampled residual table.
articles.proof: Direct substitution verifies examples; no inference about global shape from pixels.

articles.title: Two curves, how many meetings?
articles.hook: A line can meet a circle twice, once or never over R.
articles.outcome: Solve line-circle intersections by substitution and compare real and complex counts.
articles.visual: Line-circle slider with roots and discriminant table.
articles.proof: Full quadratic derivation; Bézout theorem explicitly deferred.

articles.title: Tangents from derivatives of equations
articles.hook: A curve equation hides its tangent line.
articles.outcome: Find the tangent at a smooth real point of F(x,y)=0 and detect singular-point failure.
articles.visual: Curve and gradient arrow with tangent equation readout.
articles.proof: Full first-order derivation under nonzero-gradient hypothesis; singular analysis deferred.

articles.title: When a curve has no single tangent
articles.hook: A cusp and crossing both defeat a smooth-curve rule.
articles.outcome: Classify the origin of y²=x³ and y²=x²(x+1) by local branches/tangent cones.
articles.visual: Zoomable cusp and node with branch approximations and coefficient table.
articles.proof: Full local algebra for these two examples; general singularity classification deferred.

articles.title: Where parallel lines meet
articles.hook: Affine parallel lines can meet at infinity after completion.
articles.outcome: Use homogeneous coordinates to compute a point at infinity for two parallel projective lines.
articles.visual: Affine chart z=1 and projective boundary with coordinate table.
articles.proof: Full calculation in P²; general projective geometry axioms deferred.

articles.title: Bézout for a line and a conic
articles.hook: A line and conic seem to meet twice only after careful counting.
articles.outcome: State plane Bézout with complex projective curves, no common component, and multiplicity; compute a tangent example.
articles.visual: Line-conic intersections and multiplicity table, including tangency.
articles.proof: Theorem stated, tangent example derived; general intersection-multiplicity proof deferred.

articles.title: Turn geometry into a ring
articles.hook: The same curve can be studied through polynomials on it.
articles.outcome: Construct R[x,y]/(f) for a simple curve and explain the quotient relation.
articles.visual: Parabola point and equivalent polynomial expression table.
articles.proof: Full explicit isomorphism by substitution y↦x²; general correspondence deferred.

articles.title: The Nullstellensatz in one variable
articles.hook: x and x² vanish at the same complex points but differ algebraically.
articles.outcome: State the algebraically closed-field radical ideal/zero-set correspondence and test a one-variable example.
articles.visual: Ideals (x),(x²), radical and zero-set comparison table.
articles.proof: Theorem statement and example only; Nullstellensatz proof deferred; false over R without modification.

articles.title: Why a ring can describe more than visible points
articles.hook: A polynomial relation may retain multiplicity invisible in a plot.
articles.outcome: Identify prime ideals as points of Spec A and contrast k[x]/(x²) with k[x]/(x).
articles.visual: Two ring cards with same classical point and different nilpotent arithmetic.
articles.proof: Full elementary calculation of the single prime ideal in both examples; sheaves and general schemes deferred.

articles.title: Relationships before ingredients
articles.hook: A network of composable routes is a category.
articles.outcome: Check objects, arrows, identity and associativity in the path category of a finite acyclic directed graph.
articles.visual: Finite acyclic directed graph and composition table including identities.
articles.proof: Full verification for path concatenation, including empty paths.

articles.title: Two routes, one result
articles.hook: Does processing then summarizing equal summarizing then processing?
articles.outcome: Read and verify a commuting square of finite-set functions.
articles.visual: Four finite sets, arrow maps and element-by-element table.
articles.proof: Full finite-set verification; a diagram without arrow definitions is insufficient.

articles.title: A structure-preserving translation
articles.hook: Send a collection of sets and functions into another world.
articles.outcome: Check that a functor preserves identities and composition in a concrete finite category.
articles.visual: Source and target category cards with image-arrow table.
articles.proof: Full verification for the chosen example; size issues deferred.

articles.title: A translation between translations
articles.hook: Two recipes can produce compatible answers object by object.
articles.outcome: Verify naturality for a concrete pair of functors on a finite category.
articles.visual: Naturality square with finite-value table for each arrow.
articles.proof: Full check of every generating arrow; explains why this suffices for composites.

articles.title: Pairing as a universal property
articles.hook: What makes a pair the right answer to two questions?
articles.outcome: Prove the universal property of X×Y in Set and distinguish it from its coordinate presentation.
articles.visual: Commuting triangle with unique mediator and element table.
articles.proof: Full existence and uniqueness proof in Set; products in other categories deferred.

articles.title: A pullback matches shared data
articles.hook: Join two datasets only where their keys agree.
articles.outcome: Construct a pullback in Set and prove its universal property for finite examples.
articles.visual: Two sets mapped to shared key set, matching-pair table.
articles.proof: Full existence/uniqueness proof in Set; database semantics treated as analogy.

articles.title: Free construction and forgetful map
articles.hook: A set can generate a free monoid of words.
articles.outcome: State the free-monoid/underlying-set adjunction and verify its bijection for one finite example.
articles.visual: Generator mapping extended to words, with commutative evaluation table.
articles.proof: Full extension/uniqueness proof for free monoids; general adjunction theory deferred.

articles.title: Know an object by its maps
articles.hook: An object can be probed by all arrows into it.
articles.outcome: For a locally small category C and contravariant F:C^op→Set, state Yoneda and prove one finite-category instance.
articles.visual: Probe-object arrows and element table in a small category.
articles.proof: Finite instance proved; general Yoneda proof sketched with naturality and identity arrow.

articles.title: Put processes side by side
articles.hook: Some operations compose in sequence and in parallel.
articles.outcome: Check interchange for Cartesian product of finite sets and functions, with associativity up to the canonical bijection.
articles.visual: Two string diagrams and explicit paired-input table.
articles.proof: Full verification of interchange in Set; associator isomorphisms are stated explicitly, and general coherence is deferred.

courses.title: Linear maps: a first look (selected foundations)
outcomes: Add vectors and read a 2×2 matrix as a map.
Interpret one small linear system geometrically.
courses.capstone: Design a two-step 2D transformation and explain its effect on a grid.
courses.assessment: Two worked examples, three untimed transfer problems and a written explanation of one map.

courses.title: Linear algebra refresher through geometry (selected core)
outcomes: Solve 2×2 systems and change coordinates.
Relate determinant, kernel, rank and eigenvectors.
courses.capstone: Diagnose whether a given 2×2 map is invertible and describe its eigendirections.
courses.assessment: Mixed computation and short-proof set with a counterexample to an overbroad eigenvector claim.

courses.title: Selected linear algebra proofs and applications
outcomes: Prove rank-nullity in finite dimensions.
Derive normal equations under full column rank.
Interpret a 2D singular value decomposition.
courses.capstone: Fit an inconsistent dataset and explain the residual geometry and singular values.
courses.assessment: Submit complete proofs of rank-nullity and least-squares orthogonality plus a numerical interpretation; full spectral theorem excluded.

courses.title: Geometry you can construct (selected Euclidean ideas)
outcomes: Carry out two exact constructions.
Explain why Euclidean triangle angles sum to π.
courses.capstone: Construct and justify an angle bisector and a circle-angle configuration.
courses.assessment: Untimed diagram annotations plus written congruence and parallel-line reasons.

courses.title: From Euclid to other geometries (selected models)
outcomes: Identify assumptions behind familiar theorems.
Compare spherical and disk-model geodesics.
courses.capstone: Write a comparison of one triangle theorem across Euclidean, spherical and hyperbolic settings.
courses.assessment: Model-specific calculation and assumption audit; no proof of hyperbolic consistency.

courses.title: Selected area and curvature bridges in geometry
outcomes: Prove Euclidean angle and circle claims.
Compute Pick area and a hyperbolic triangle defect under stated model assumptions.
courses.capstone: Compare one lattice polygon area with one hyperbolic triangle area, stating why the formulas measure different geometries.
courses.assessment: Written proofs for classical claims and a conditional Gauss–Bonnet application; full hyperbolic metric development excluded.

courses.title: Topology through intervals and surfaces (selected gateway)
outcomes: Test openness for simple subsets of R with an epsilon interval.
Compute Euler characteristic for simple closed triangulated surfaces without treating it as a complete invariant.
courses.capstone: Test whether two subsets of R are open, then count V,E,F on two triangulations of a sphere.
courses.assessment: Definitions check, explicit boundary counterexample and labelled Euler counts; no topological equivalence inferred from animation.

courses.title: Topology refresher with explicit hypotheses (selected core)
outcomes: Use open-preimage continuity.
Prove connected-image and interval-compactness claims.
courses.capstone: Compare circle and closed interval using a topological invariant and justify every property invoked.
courses.assessment: Two full short proofs, counterexample search and an untimed quotient-space explanation.

courses.title: Selected topology proofs and loop invariants
outcomes: Prove selected compactness and connectedness theorems.
Use winding number and the circle fundamental-group statement with lifting assumptions.
courses.capstone: Write a proof dossier for one point-set result and a conditional winding-number argument.
courses.assessment: Full proofs for point-set tasks; loop task must identify the deferred lifting lemma and may not claim a complete π₁ proof.

courses.title: Symmetry and modular arithmetic (selected group gateway)
outcomes: Check a group operation on a square or clock.
Find inverses and element orders in finite examples.
courses.capstone: Build the square-symmetry composition table and identify one noncommuting pair.
courses.assessment: Operation-table check and two short axiom justifications.

courses.title: Groups and rings refresher (selected core)
outcomes: Use cosets and homomorphisms.
Distinguish rings from fields in modular examples.
courses.capstone: Explain why Z/7Z supports division by every nonzero residue while Z/6Z does not.
courses.assessment: Short proofs of Lagrange and prime-field criterion plus counterexamples to false converses.

courses.title: Selected group and ring proofs
outcomes: Prove quotient-group well-definedness under normality.
Use ideal and field arguments in Z and Z/nZ.
State the scope of Sylow without claiming its proof.
courses.capstone: Construct two quotients and explain which relations are collapsed and why the operations are well-defined.
courses.assessment: Full proofs for Lagrange, quotient and prime-field claims; Sylow is assessed as theorem interpretation only.

courses.title: Curves that bend (selected calculus geometry)
outcomes: Calculate length of a parametrized curve.
Interpret curvature for a circle and a line.
courses.capstone: Compare two parametrizations of the same circular arc and their lengths.
courses.assessment: Calculation, units check and a short explanation of regularity.

courses.title: From curves to surfaces (selected foundations)
outcomes: Compute local metric coefficients.
Identify regular surface patches and geodesic candidates.
courses.capstone: Compute a sphere-patch metric and compare lengths of two candidate routes.
courses.assessment: Derivative checks, metric calculation and a written warning about pole coordinates.

courses.title: Selected curvature and Gauss–Bonnet applications
outcomes: Compute Gaussian curvature in selected patches.
Apply Gauss–Bonnet with orientation and compactness hypotheses.
Explain one spherical holonomy calculation.
courses.capstone: Derive the octant area/holonomy relation and state precisely which theorem is being invoked.
courses.assessment: Local metric and curvature calculations plus a conditional theorem application; general Gauss–Bonnet proof excluded.

courses.title: Polynomial pictures with exact checks (selected gateway)
outcomes: Plot and verify real polynomial zero sets.
Find line-circle intersections with an equation.
courses.capstone: Analyze a one-parameter line-circle family, including tangent and no-real-point cases by discriminant.
courses.assessment: Exact substitution and discriminant reasoning; plots are exploratory evidence only.

courses.title: Curves, singularities and projective points (selected core)
outcomes: Distinguish smooth and singular points.
Compute a simple projective point at infinity.
State Bézout with its required hypotheses.
courses.capstone: Audit a claimed curve-intersection count for missing complex, projective and multiplicity assumptions.
courses.assessment: Exact computations and theorem-scope critique; no full Bézout proof.

courses.title: Affine algebraic geometry windows (selected foundations)
outcomes: Build a coordinate-ring isomorphism in a concrete example.
Use radical ideals to distinguish set and scheme-level information.
Compute Spec for one nilpotent ring.
courses.capstone: Compare k[x]/(x) and k[x]/(x²): classical points, ideals and nilpotents, with k algebraically closed.
courses.assessment: Full explicit ring calculations; Nullstellensatz and general schemes are theorem statements with deferred proofs.

courses.title: Arrows and diagrams (selected category gateway)
outcomes: Check identities and associative composition in a path category.
Verify a commuting square by values.
Test one finite functor for preservation of identities and composition.
courses.capstone: Build a four-object finite diagram and check whether two routes agree.
courses.assessment: Element-by-element diagram checks, a short associativity argument and a finite-functor verification; abstract applications excluded.

courses.title: Functors and universal properties (selected core)
outcomes: Verify a functor and natural transformation.
Prove the product property in Set.
courses.capstone: Construct a pullback of finite-set functions and prove its mediator is unique.
courses.assessment: Commuting-diagram verification and full existence/uniqueness proof.

courses.title: Selected universal constructions in Set and Mon
outcomes: Prove Set product and pullback universal properties.
Explain free-monoid adjunction.
Interpret a finite Yoneda instance and its variance.
courses.capstone: Write a small proof dossier comparing product, pullback and free-monoid universal arrows.
courses.assessment: Full proofs for Set/Mon constructions; finite Yoneda proof plus clearly labelled general sketch.

labs.title: Matrix grid studio
controls: four matrix entries as numeric fields and arrow keys
labs.readout: Mapped basis vectors, input/output coordinate table, determinant and signed unit-square area.
labs.invariant: For every vector v=x e1+y e2, Av=x Ae1+y Ae2; area scale equals |det A|.
labs.pitfalls: Singular maps collapse area; negative determinant reverses orientation; sliders alone cannot certify a general theorem.
labs.accessibleFallback: Keyboard fields, tabular point samples and an SVG-free text walkthrough of each transformed basis vector.

labs.title: Eigenlines and ellipse
labs.readout: Av, eigenvalue candidates, singular values and sampled unit-circle image.
labs.invariant: For real A, squared singular values equal eigenvalues of AᵀA.
labs.pitfalls: A real rotation may have no real eigenvectors; eigenvectors and singular vectors differ.
labs.accessibleFallback: Numeric table of sampled vectors and an announced no-real-eigenvector state.

labs.title: Compass construction bench
labs.readout: Equal radii, triangle side lengths and final angle comparison.
labs.invariant: The bisector construction relies on equal radii and SSS congruence.
labs.pitfalls: Degenerate zero angle and imprecise pixel intersections must not be presented as exact proof.
labs.accessibleFallback: Numbered construction instructions with a labelled congruence table.

labs.title: Three triangle models
labs.readout: Model, geodesic definition, three angles, angle sum and area when supported.
labs.invariant: Euclidean sum π; sphere octant example 3π/2; hyperbolic curvature −1 area equals defect.
labs.pitfalls: Screen-circle arcs are not Euclidean straight lines; disk boundary is infinitely far away; numerical angles are approximate.
labs.accessibleFallback: Preset exact examples and a text table of model-specific claims, assumptions and computed angles.

labs.title: Epsilon-neighborhood tester
labs.readout: Membership, neighborhood containment and counterexample point when available.
labs.invariant: An open set in R gives each of its points some contained epsilon interval.
labs.pitfalls: Passing finitely many samples does not prove openness; boundary points need exact tests.
labs.accessibleFallback: Keyboard-selectable standard sets and symbolic interval inclusion table.

labs.title: Triangulation counter
labs.readout: V, E, F, χ and a labelled edge-identification table.
labs.invariant: For a closed triangulated surface, allowed subdivision preserves V−E+F.
labs.pitfalls: Nonmanifold gluing, missing faces or boundary changes interpretation; χ alone does not classify all spaces.
labs.accessibleFallback: Text list of vertices, edges and faces with count deltas after each subdivision.

labs.title: Square symmetry composer
labs.readout: Image of labelled vertices, composition result, inverse and order.
labs.invariant: Composition of square symmetries stays in D4; associative law comes from function composition.
labs.pitfalls: Order matters for a reflection and rotation; an animation is not a group-axiom proof.
labs.accessibleFallback: Keyboard-operated selectors with full permutation and Cayley-table row readout.

labs.title: Modular arithmetic workbench
labs.readout: Residue table, additive inverse, multiplicative inverse if any and gcd(a,n).
labs.invariant: A nonzero residue is invertible mod n exactly when gcd(a,n)=1.
labs.pitfalls: Modulus 1 is excluded from field claim; zero divisors appear for composite n.
labs.accessibleFallback: Plain table of all residue operations and a text Euclidean-algorithm trace.

labs.title: Curve curvature microscope
labs.readout: Position, unit tangent, signed curvature and cumulative arc length.
labs.invariant: For regular C² curves, signed curvature is det(γ′,γ″)/||γ′||³ and is unchanged by orientation-preserving reparameterization.
labs.pitfalls: At zero speed curvature formula is undefined; graph appearance depends on aspect ratio.
labs.accessibleFallback: Numeric derivative table, formula substitution and named regularity status.

labs.title: Sphere path measurer
labs.readout: Metric coefficients, path length estimate, exact great-circle central angle when applicable.
labs.invariant: For sphere radius R, great-circle arc length is R times central angle for the shorter arc.
labs.pitfalls: Latitude circles except equator are not geodesics; coordinate poles are singular.
labs.accessibleFallback: Coordinate-free dot-product central-angle calculation and a segment-length table.

labs.title: Polynomial zero-set explorer
labs.readout: Residual F(x,y), gradient when defined, exact special-point checks.
labs.invariant: Displayed real points satisfy F=0 to stated numerical tolerance; exact named examples use symbolic substitution.
labs.pitfalls: Pixel absence is not proof of no zeros; near singularities numerical gradients mislead.
labs.accessibleFallback: Preset equations, symbolic sample calculations and a coordinate table of verified points.

labs.title: Line and conic intersections
labs.readout: Roots, discriminant, homogeneous point at infinity and intersection multiplicity for the preset tangency.
labs.invariant: Line and conic have total intersection multiplicity two over complex projective plane if no component is shared.
labs.pitfalls: Real affine plot can hide complex or infinite intersections; the full Bézout theorem is not proved by the widget.
labs.accessibleFallback: Exact polynomial elimination and roots table with multiplicity and chart labels.

labs.title: Commuting diagram checker
labs.readout: Both path outputs for every element and the first mismatch.
labs.invariant: A finite-set square commutes iff the two composites agree on every input element.
labs.pitfalls: One tested element cannot establish equality of functions; arrow domains/codomains must match.
labs.accessibleFallback: Fully keyboard-controlled function tables with a row-by-row equality verdict.

labs.title: Pullback matching table
controls: functions f and g as tables
labs.readout: All pairs (x,y) with f(x)=g(y), projection maps and candidate mediator.
labs.invariant: The Set pullback contains exactly compatible pairs and each compatible cone has a unique mediator.
labs.pitfalls: Database join analogy omits bag semantics and missing values; avoid claiming all joins are pullbacks.
labs.accessibleFallback: Text matching-pair table and stepwise universal-property proof using an arbitrary element.
